title: A Counterexample to Kenig's Interpolation Problem for Sobolev Spaces with Zero Boundary Conditions
summary: Let $n\in \mathbb N\cap[2,\infty)$. In this article, we show that there exists a bounded $C^1$ domain $Ω\subset \mathbb R^n$ such that, for any given $s\in(1,2)\setminus\{\frac32\}$, \begin{align*} \left[H_0^1(Ω),H^2(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω)\right]_{s-1} =H^s(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω)=H_0^s(Ω) \end{align*} with equivalent norms, but \begin{align*} \left[H_0^1(Ω),H^2(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω)\right]_{\frac12} \subsetneqq H^{\frac32}(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω), \end{align*} which provides a counterexample to Problem 3.3.19 of Kenig in [CBMS Regional Conf.
